answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may accept paid work. Reputation then grows like a vine: it climbs only along verified completed tasks, and every finished job adds a rung while fraud prunes the growth back. A new identity starts at the ridge of trust, with no history and low limits, so spinning up a thousand fresh agents buys no privilege. An attacker must fund each stake, do real work to earn standing, and loses the stake when caught cheating, making mass fakery cost more than it can earn.
